To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. In general, optimising a metric M on a training set is not a good guide to how the metric will perform on a test set, even though the test set is drawn from the same distribution as the training set.
1. The choice of metric for optimising a ranking algorithm is a complex issue, and there is a danger of making the wrong choice.

(1) the usual assumption is not self evident, (2) there are good reasons to believe that in many cases the usual assumption is false, and (3) there are good practical reasons to believe that the usual assumption is likely to be false for the case of the evaluation metric M being the Mean Average Precision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given a set of labeled data, and a set of possible ranking functions, how do we select the ranking function which best predicts the live ranking?
the following question: What are the consequences of the fact that the training data is not drawn from the same environment as that in which we wish to apply our model?
the following questions: (i) How well does optimising an evaluation metric on a test set correlate with optimising the same evaluation metric on the live environment?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it is not a good general rule, but it may be a good rule in certain circumstances.
it is not a good idea to assume that the metric M that is best for the live environment is the same as the metric M that gives the best performance on a training set.
it is often better not to optimise exactly for the metric M, and that there may be other approaches to optimisation that are better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we should be careful about the choice of metric, that we should be prepared to use a metric which is not the same as the live metric, and that we should be aware that the training set might not be a reliable guide to how the algorithm will behave in the live environment.
the usual optimisation strategy is not necessarily a good one, and there are alternative strategies that may work better in some situations.
